# A template written as a Go string literal reports where it sits in the
# Go file that holds it, so the position addresses real bytes there and
# not an offset inside the template text.

check-templates -definitions
stdout 'main\.go:9:58\+21\t"greeting"\t.*main\.go:9:81\+7\t.*main\.go:9:67\+10'
! stderr .

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.25.0
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"html/template"
	"net/http"
)

var templates = template.Must(template.New("app").Parse(`{{define "greeting"}}Hi{{end}}`))

type Page struct {
	Title string
}

func handleIndex(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	_ = templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "greeting", Page{Title: "Home"})
}

var _ = fmt.Sprint
